before.label: Oral history
before.description: Oral history creates and interprets testimony through interviews, archives and collaborative projects. Recorded accounts illuminate events, memory and narrative, while the interviewer, editing and social relations shape the evidence.

added.citation: Paul Thompson, The Voice of the Past: Oral History, second edition (1988), extracted as “The Voice of the Past: Oral history,” reader chapter 2, 33–39.

verification.note: Complete seven-page excerpt read. Editorial credit identifies 1988 second edition; later headnote and page numbers belong to the reader, not the original. Explicit omissions remain. Supports social purpose, interview selection and qualifications of community participation; no full book, original-page collation or comprehensive methods check. His broad historiographical judgments remain attributed, not adopted as settled descriptions.

added.title: Michael Frisch, “Preparing Interview Transcripts for Documentary Publication: A Line-by-Line Illustration of the Editing Process,” in A Shared Authority (1990), 81–146; methodological introduction, 81–88.
added.citation: Michael Frisch, “Preparing Interview Transcripts for Documentary Publication: A Line-by-Line Illustration of the Editing Process,” in A Shared Authority (1990), 81–146; methodological introduction, 81–88.

verification.note: Complete methodological introduction 81–88 read in public transcription. Edited interview 89–91 and part of 92 encountered; full edited/source transcript comparison 89–146 not completed. No audio or scan collation. Supports Frisch’s editorial rationale, project collaboration and stated omissions, not an independent audit of editing fidelity. The Social Research version was tailored to its 1987 unemployment issue; the source transcript printed here itself omits wholly excised sections.

outcomes.finding: Primary Thompson and Frisch passages now support qualified accounts of community participation, selection, audience and documentary editing. Rogovin and Hughes receive named contribution records.
outcomes.research_limit: Thompson: complete seven-page reader excerpt 33–39, explicitly credited to the 1988 second edition, read with its visible omissions. Later editorial headnote not backdated; original book pages not collated, full book unread. Frisch: complete methodological introduction to chapter 5, 81–88, read in public transcription. Edited interview 89–91 and partial 92 also encountered, but the complete edited/source demonstration 89–146 was not compared. No audio or scan collation. The chapter itself notes omissions even from its source transcript. Records support his rationale and project credits, not an independent certification of editorial fidelity. Women’s Words chapters remain unread; the frozen question allowed Frisch as the alternative.
